record.original_question: How can mathematical biology reach the level of mathematical maturity needed for living systems by developing rigorous biological definitions, using theorem-proof style arguments where appropriate, and creating genuinely new mathematical theory rather than relying mainly on imported or ad hoc methods?

evidence.quote: Mathematical biology requires new mathematical theory [103], and the passive importation of mathematical models from other fields, particularly physics and engineering, and their application in superficial ways to biological systems runs counter to the constructive progression of mathematical and theoretical biology.
There is, we feel, increasing need of employing the definition-theorem-proof style of mathematics in mathematical biology.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Develop a programmatic framework for raising the mathematical maturity of the study of living systems. Specifically, propose how to: (i) formulate rigorous, intrinsically biological definitions (of objects such as cell, organism, population, fitness, function, regulation, adaptation) suitable to serve as primitive notions in a definition–theorem–proof style theory; (ii) identify settings within mathematical biology in which theorem–proof arguments can replace heuristic or simulation-based reasoning, and exhibit prototypical theorems with complete proofs; and (iii) construct genuinely new mathematical theory tailored to biological phenomena, rather than relying on the direct importation of techniques from physics, engineering, or other established fields. Provide criteria by which such a framework can be judged successful and demonstrate its application to at least one substantive biological question.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a programmatic, foundational research direction rather than a precisely formulated mathematical conjecture, and no resolution is reported in the literature; it remains an open challenge for the field.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems in mathematical biology, including calls for new mathematical theory and rigorous foundational definitions.
status_evidence.claim: The challenge is posed as an open problem and not as a resolved result.
